According to Table S1, the leaching of nickel, manganese, and cobalt into the Cyrene during separation was as follows:

| Element | Before separation (wt%) | After separation (wt%) |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Ni | 13.4 | 13.2 |
| Mn | 5.5 | 5.5 |
| Co | 1.2 | 1.1 |

The paper states that the ether groups in the Cyrene molecule caused lithium leaching, not nickel, manganese, or cobalt leaching. However, it is likely that the leaching of lithium also caused the leaching of other cations, such as nickel, manganese, and cobalt, due to their similar ionic radii and charge.
